Subject: Capacity phasing & SLA — initial proposal

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our engineering and procurement teams reviewed the usage profile you shared. We need to propose a phased capacity add: an initial reserved block for pilot (Q1) with a staged uplift over the next 12 months tied to specific throughput milestones.

Key asks from CloudHaven:
- A 3-month pilot block (reserve 25k token units/month) with an opt-in to expand to 100k by month 13.
- A clear SLA lane for burst capacity (99.9% availability for baseline, 95% for burst) and a defined credit mechanism if burst capacity is delayed.
- Pricing that prorates between pilot and committed phases (we expect a mid-contract price band reset).

Attached: CloudHaven_Proposed_SOW_v1.pdf (contains proposed schedule and milestone triggers).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can support phased reservations and what the change-order path looks like from your side? Also cc'ing our legal lead Maya for redline coordination.

Ari Patel
Head of Procurement, CloudHaven Technologies

Ari — thanks for the clear summary and the SOW. We can support phased reservations and define a formal change order path. High level:

- Pilot block: we can reserve the 25k token/month pool for a 3-month pilot with standard pilot pricing (creditable to committed once you convert).
- Uplift: we can architect an incremental order form schedule that triggers on milestone acceptance tests (the SOW milestones look fine, will confirm exact acceptance language).
- SLA/credits: Redwood has a documented SLA credit table for capacity shortfalls; for burst we usually provide a graded credit (partial credit if we miss 95–99% and larger credit below 95%).

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal redline from our commercial/legal to the SOW (Karthik and Laura to lead).
2) Joint redline review with CloudHaven legal (Maya) next week.
3) Draft a single change order template (MSA appendix + order form) so future uplifts are one sign-off.

Karthik/Laura — can you take point on the redlines? I'll coordinate schedule with CloudHaven.

Team —

Attached are our suggested commercial and SOW redlines. High-level comments:
- Move milestone acceptance to a deterministic test (90th pct latency threshold on a seeded test harness) rather than vague "engineering sign-off." This avoids subjective stalls.
- Instead of a hard price reset at month 13, propose an indexed band tied to committed throughput and a one-time reconciliation at month 13.
- For burst availability, propose a stepped credit: 10% credit if burst availability <99% for the month, 25% credit if <95%. We also propose a 72-hour notice window for planned maintenance that affects burst lanes.

I've put edits into Redwood_COA_redlines_20261102.docx (commercial terms + SOW markup). Laura — please double-check the invoicing/proration language; Ari/Maya, happy to walk through the doc during a sync.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference

Karthik, Jordan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few counterpoints from CloudHaven legal:
- The acceptance test needs to include production-like dataset validation to ensure model behavior under our traffic patterns. We can agree to a seeded harness, but want an additional field test window (7 days) before milestone acceptance.
- For price indexing, we prefer an annual review with an express floor to prevent mid-contract price creep.
- SLA credits are acceptable in principle; we will ask for a one-time "grace allotment" for the first 60 days post-pilot conversion to account for tuning and KV-cache warmup.

We can review during a 30-minute legal sync on Wed (Nov 4). Please share your availability.

Maya Singh
Senior Counsel, CloudHaven Technologies
